title: Element names of the delivery fact and of the notice answer are not in the sources read for this work package
description: The legacy story names the WIN file, the acknowledgment and the proof read by Java interfaces and by the ACE views, and the target contract of the key is RWB-P6-E1055-CON. The JSON element names of rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1 and of the notice read of rwb-comms are not stated in any source read for this work package, so this story uses the element names it writes and fixes them at contract review, without changing a value or a rule.
evidence: RWB-E1-055 section 12 lists WinFileGateway.send, WinAcknowledgmentHandler.onAcknowledgment, InteractionLedgerApi.record and RecoveryDataApi.proofOfDelivery with no element names; the P6 slice publishes NoticeDelivered with the delivery status and the call-back date but names no JSON fields.
proposed: Confirm the element names of the two rows in RWB-P6-E1055-CON at contract review and rename in this story if they differ; no value, rule, criterion or test changes.

title: No warning point is defined for a notice period
source: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 timer; LOV-TIMER; RWB-E1-055 section 8
description: The timer table carries warn_at and DF-WRK-041 warned_at, and the service-level clock derives its warning point from the warning percent of its row. No source read for this work package gives a warning point, a warning percentage or a warning message for a NOTICE_PERIOD timer, so the story writes warn_at as null and claims no warning for this clock rather than inventing one.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 timer: warn_at (DF-WRK-033) and warned_at (DF-WRK-041) are optional columns; the warning of RWB-E1-028 is bound to the SERVICE_LEVEL row and MSG-P3-003, and no row of the sources binds either to NOTICE_PERIOD.
proposed: If a warning is wanted on the notice period, load a warning percentage or a warning day count as a reference row of rwb-case and add one criterion; until then warn_at stays null.

title: Whether a deviation pauses a statutory notice period is not settled by the sources
source: Architecture v5 slide 3 notes; Business Rules R-DEV-01, R-UNI-43; RWB-E1-055 sections 8 and 9
description: R-DEV-01 pauses the stage clock and never the legal prescription clock, and Architecture v5 slide 3 says the legal deadline never pauses. A notice period is a statutory period on which a court relies, but no source read for this work package states that a deviation leaves the notice period running, and no source states that it pauses it either. The story takes the reading that the clock is a legal clock and is never paused, and records the opposite reading as open.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 3: dispute, hardship, death, fraud, bankruptcy, lost contact and damaged collateral pause the case clock; the legal deadline never pauses. RWB-E1-055 sections 8 and 9 say nothing about a deviation.
proposed: Keep the notice period unpaused as ASM-B2-P3-016-3 records; if Legal rules that it pauses, the deviation contract gains one signal to the notice clock and one criterion changes.

title: The timer has no field for the notice it belongs to, and its field ID is unallocated
source: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 timer; RWB-E1-055 section 11
description: The legacy story writes the notice reference on the notice row of the P6 module, and the ownership map gives the timer table to rwb-case with id, case_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at, warn_at, paused, status, escalation_level, warned_at, treatment_id, escalated_to_role and escalated_at. A notice period that cannot name its notice is of no use in a court pack, so the story adds one nullable column and one index; the Data Dictionary field ID for that column is not allocated in any source read here.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 lists DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036, DF-WRK-041 to DF-WRK-044 for timer with no reference column; RWB-E1-055 section 11 reads DF-LEG-015 notice.id and DF-LEG-016 notice.case_id only.
owner_role: rwb-case data owner and the Data Dictionary owner
proposed: Allocate the field ID in the Logical Data Model and add it to the ownership map at the next revision; the column, its type and its index stand as written.

title: The notice period is owned by two rwb-case stories of the same legacy loop
source: RWB-E1-055 sections 4, 9 and 10; RWB-P3-E5002-APP; this story
description: Legacy RWB-E1-055 assigns the notice-period clock to P3 and names the delivered date as its start, and the Epics 3 to 8 set already carries RWB-P3-E5002-APP, which starts the same clock from the delivery answer of rwb-litigation at wave 3. Both readings are correct for their own fact and the sources do not settle which one owns the row when both facts arrive for one notice, so this story is recorded as a secondary slice that owns no legacy criterion, and the partial unique index and the business key make the second fact a repeat counted under R-UNI-40.
evidence: RWB-E1-055 section 9: P3 starts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer when it consumes NoticeDelivered (EV-15). RWB-P3-E5002-APP section 1: it creates or does not create the notice-period timer from the S4 delivery answer.
proposed: Keep both facts with the one clock, the unique running index and the idempotency key of notice and delivered date; revisit at the wave 3 refinement of RWB-P3-E5002-APP.

title: The role that receives the expiry of a notice period is not named
source: RWB-E1-055 section 10; TSD P3 v3 T6.1; RWB-P3-E1028-APP
description: The legacy authority table gives RW-LITOFF the read of the notice state and gives the platform administrator the job monitor, and it names no receiver for the end of a notice period. The timers story of the service publishes TimerBreached with the escalation role of the SERVICE_LEVEL row in force, so this story reuses that mechanism; a case whose queue and status have no SERVICE_LEVEL row would expire with no receiver, and that case is not covered by any source read here.
evidence: RWB-E1-055 section 10 lists SY-DATALOAD, SY-CASEWF, RW-LITOFF, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PLATADM and RW-DATASTEW with no expiry receiver; RWB-P3-E1028-APP BR3 takes the role from the SERVICE_LEVEL row.
proposed: Take the escalation role from the SERVICE_LEVEL row in force as ASM-B2-P3-016-6 records, and add a named default role for a missing row if the business lead asks for one.
